_comment: The registry entry shape UIS reads for an APPLICATION. This is the seam
Only the fields UIS actually reads are marked required below. Everything
else in a real entry is display metadata for the website and for
`uis template info`, and UIS neither requires nor validates it.

categories.name: Data Applications
categories._note: context MUST be "uis" or the entry is invisible to `uis template list`. An application in a dct-context category is still listed, but only because template.sh accepts templateKind: application unconditionally as a safety net - do not rely on that.

templates.name: Atlas
templates.description: Norwegian kommune data, ingested by Dagster and served as a REST API

_required.templateKind: Must be the literal "application". UIS reads `.templateKind // .kind`; the registry already has BOTH templateKind and install_type, so reuse one rather than adding a third discriminator. install refuses an entry it cannot classify BEFORE fetching anything.
_required.source.artifact: The OCI artifact holding the install definition - by convention <image>/uis, published beside the image at the same tag. NOT the application image itself. Must match the allowlist: ghcr.io/helpers-no/* or ghcr.io/terchris/* by default.
_required.source.tag: What the pin was published as. Shown to a human; NEVER pulled by. Refused if it is latest, main, master, head or empty.
_required.source.digest: What UIS actually pulls. sha256: plus 64 hex. An entry with no digest is refused, because a tag alone is not a pin. 🔴 AUTHORED, NOT RESOLVED BY THE BUILD: a catalogue build that re-resolves the tag on every run tracks the tag, so a tag re-pointed at a different artifact is blessed by the next unrelated build - and UIS reads the latest published registry and pins no version of it, so nothing downstream can tell. Pulling a digest gives integrity; only a committed, reviewable digest gives provenance. Established by dev-templates on urb-agents#479 against an earlier claim of mine.
_required.visibility: public | private. TOP-LEVEL - a sibling of source, NOT a member of it. Nested, UIS reads null and defaults to public, which works until the first private artifact fails by never asking for credentials. Decides whether the pull needs `oras login`; on a private artifact with no credentials the error names the SECRET, not the URL.
_required.category: Must reference a category whose context is "uis", or the entry will not appear in `uis template list`.

_not_read_by_uis: folder, templateRepoPath, files, filesMdx - a stack template's fields; an application has no folder
params, provides - these come from the ARTIFACT's template-info.yaml, which is the single source of truth. If the registry inlines a resolved copy for the website, UIS still reads the artifact.
logo, readme, links, maintainers, prerequisites, quickstart, architectureMdx, expectedOutputBlock
